source_snapshot.procedure: Run raw App 0x06 0x38 <Channel number> <Requested privilege level> over localhost IB and remote OOB; privilege 1 Callback, 2 User, 3 Operator, 4 Administrator, 5 OEM; compare with `ipmitool channel authcap`; generic logs are cleared first.
source_snapshot.criteria: Commands succeed and raw response meaning equals the high-level authcap output.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL incorrectly treats the standard raw request as implementation-specific and awaits exact output instead of applying the normative bitfield schema.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: FULLY AUTOMATABLE correctly requires input validation and semantic raw/high-level comparison, but does not distinguish the source's legacy bit7=0 request from ipmitool's extended-first request/fallback or preserve the listed privilege matrix explicitly.

old_problem: The historical record retained Pending for channel/privilege, response masks and a protected tool. IPMI v2.0 Table 22-15 fully defines both request bytes and the eight response data bytes, and the pinned ipmitool implementation documents its extended-first then legacy fallback. Only target channel coverage and secret-safe execution are runtime Project bindings; no unknown OEM command is required unless OEM authentication is reported.
disposition_reason: Keep raw 0x06/0x38 on both IB/OOB and the high-level `channel authcap` comparison. For every approved explicit channel, run privilege subcases 1-5. Preserve the source legacy request with channel bit7 clear, add a standard extended-data request with bit7 set so ipmitool's extended output can be compared correctly, decode all fields and reserved bits, and normalize semantics rather than display text. Remove log clearing and plaintext credentials; no configuration command or orchestration retry is allowed.
decision_basis: XLSX row 1014, same-row DeepSeek, exact GPT V2, tests JSON, selection manifest, historical V3.1 record and adjacent row 1015 were directly read; next pending was verified as Functionality row 1015 / variant 5653b172749853db.

IPMI v2.0 section 22.13 and Table 22-15 define App 0x38 as unauthenticated capability discovery. Request byte 1 is bit7 extended-data request plus channel 0-B/F or E current; request byte 2 is privilege 1 Callback through 5 OEM.

The successful response contains eight data bytes after completion: actual channel, Authentication Type Support, authentication/user status, extended protocol support, three-byte little-endian OEM IANA and OEM auxiliary data. Reserved bits have normative zero behavior.

With request bit7 clear, the compatibility response suppresses extended indications; with bit7 set, bit7 of Authentication Type Support announces extended data and the KG/IPMI-version fields become meaningful. These variants must not be compared as if their raw bytes were identical.

Pinned ipmitool `channel authcap` sets request channel bit7 first and, on no response or nonzero completion, issues one legacy fallback. A single audited high-level invocation may therefore represent either standard variant; the wrapper must record which semantics it returned and the test harness must not add another retry.

ED-02, ED-03, ED-13, ED-15, ED-19, ED-22, ED-26 through ED-30 and ED-33 through ED-38 preserve transport/privilege coverage, require exact evidence and pass criteria, permit runtime parameterization, preserve logs and forbid hidden assumptions or blind retry.

test_case.test_name: Verify Channel Authentication Capabilities across transports, privileges and legacy/extended views
test_case.purpose: For each Project-approved explicit BMC messaging channel and requested privilege 1-5, prove standard legacy and extended Get Channel Authentication Capabilities decode correctly, agree across IB/OOB, and correlate with the pinned high-level ipmitool view without changing channel, authentication, users, logs, host or BMC state.
required_package: Immutable DUT/host/BMC/local-interface mapping, firmware identity, pinned ipmitool be11d948 and protected OOB secret injection

Versioned Project channel matrix containing explicit numeric target channels; use 0x0-0xB or 0xF as platform-defined, and do not use 0xE when comparing IB/OOB because it means the channel carrying each request

Coverage matrix executing requested privileges 0x01 Callback, 0x02 User, 0x03 Operator, 0x04 Administrator and 0x05 OEM for every approved channel; record a Project-SPEC N/A only where truly inapplicable
Table 22-15 parser/normalizer validating exactly eight response data bytes, channel echo, every reserved bit, auth-type mask, status flags, extended support, little-endian OEM IANA and auxiliary data

Audited high-level authcap wrapper that records extended success versus the pinned implementation's single legacy fallback, stores protected raw/high-level evidence and performs no harness-level retry
test_case.test_command:
READ-ONLY PROCEDURE; DO NOT EXECUTE DURING REVIEW. Bind IB/OOB to the same BMC, preserve logs and expand the approved channel-by-privilege matrix. For each `,

`, validate explicit channel and p in 1..5. On both transports issue the source-preserved legacy request `ipmitool raw 0x06 0x38

` and separately the extended request `ipmitool raw 0x06 0x38

` exactly once. Require completion success and exactly eight returned data bytes; validate actual channel, reserved bits and all Table 22-15 fields. Legacy requests must obey compatibility suppression; extended requests must decode the advertised capability state. Run the pinned `ipmitool channel authcap

` once under an audited wrapper on each transport, record whether its built-in extended-first path succeeded or used its one legacy fallback, normalize the displayed fields and compare them only with the matching raw variant. Compare IB/OOB for the same explicit channel/privilege/variant. Never use the example channel 2/admin as a default, use current-channel 0xE for cross-path equality, clear logs, expose credentials, invoke channel/user/password setters, create a session, or add an automatic retry.
test_case.expected_result: Every configured channel/privilege subcase returns a structurally valid eight-byte capability record. The returned channel equals the explicit request; reserved bits are zero; legacy and extended fields obey their requested form; IB and OOB normalized capabilities match for each form; and the audited high-level output equals the corresponding raw decode including auth types, authentication status, username/anonymous state, version support and OEM metadata. No setting or log changes.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires complete approved channel coverage and privileges 1-5, both transports, both legacy/extended standard forms, success plus exact length, correct returned channel, zero reserved bits, complete field decoding, same-variant IB/OOB equality, recorded high-level route and field-for-field semantic equality. Command success alone, textual comparison, example values, current-channel 0xE across different transports, comparing legacy suppression against extended bytes, unknown OEM meaning, missing privilege subcase, hidden fallback, extra retry or any mutation cannot pass. Unsupported/N/A needs Project SPEC; a completion or empty bitmask alone is not N/A.
safety_gate: Read only: allow App 0x38 and high-level authcap only; prohibit channel access/authentication, user, password, session, log, reset and power changes.
Verify exact target and explicit channel on both transports. Do not use 0xE in a cross-transport comparison and do not assume the source example channel 2 is the LAN channel.

Treat authentication capabilities, anonymous/null-user status, KG state and OEM metadata as security-sensitive evidence; protect credentials and apply approved redaction without losing comparison hashes.
The pinned high-level tool's documented extended-to-legacy fallback must be visible in the audit. The harness never retries a failed raw or high-level subcase.
On malformed/short data, nonzero completion, reserved bits, path mismatch or unrecognized OEM data, preserve the first evidence, stop that subcase and escalate; do not repair configuration.
expected_evidence: Target/firmware/interface/tool commit, explicit channel matrix, privilege 1-5 coverage and protected credential policy
For every matrix entry and transport: exact legacy and extended request bytes, completion/exit, eight raw data bytes or first failure and timestamps
Structured actual-channel, auth-type, KG, per-message/user-level auth, username/anonymous, IPMI v1.5/v2.0, OEM IANA/aux and reserved-bit decode
Audited high-level request route including any built-in legacy fallback, normalized output and matching-variant raw comparison
IB/OOB semantic comparisons, per-subcase verdicts, aggregate coverage proof and non-mutation/no-extra-retry audit
test_case.recovery: No state change is expected and no corrective operation is authorized. On any failure, stop the affected subcase after its first bounded evidence capture, retain protected raw/high-level data and identify target, channel, transport, parser, fallback or firmware discrepancy. Do not change channel/auth/user/password settings, clear logs, create a session, reset/power cycle or retry automatically.

source_conflict.reason: The source raw command and semantic high-level comparison are valid. The Review layer supplies the normative schema, distinguishes legacy from extended bit7 behavior and removes unsafe log/credential handling without changing protected source text.

blocked.reason: All standard request/response fields and the pinned high-level fallback are defined. Exact target channels and applicable coverage are finite runtime Project configuration; OEM data is reported but not guessed.
